question: Should Discord Activity support continue from this older draft branch, move to the newer broader Discord Activities PR, or restart as a Canvas-plugin-owned design with fail-closed Activity auth?
rationale: The unresolved choice crosses plugin ownership, Gateway authorization, token transport, operator config shape, and two overlapping dirty branches, so automation can identify blockers but should not choose the permanent Activity security boundary.

options.title: Rebuild under Canvas plugin auth
options.body: Port Activity config, routing, and A2UI bridge behavior into `extensions/canvas` and `extensions/discord`, require credentials or a verifiable exchange, avoid URL tokens, bound fanout, and add live Discord proof.

options.title: Continue through the newer PR
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/65205 as the working branch only after its similar security, compatibility, proof, and merge-state blockers are resolved.

options.title: Pause the feature
options.body: Keep Discord Activities out of core until maintainers settle the Activity auth model and whether this belongs in the Canvas plugin or an external package.

recommendation.title: Rebuild under Canvas plugin auth
recommendation.body: Port Activity config, routing, and A2UI bridge behavior into `extensions/canvas` and `extensions/discord`, require credentials or a verifiable exchange, avoid URL tokens, bound fanout, and add live Discord proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision is primarily about Gateway auth, config migration, and Canvas plugin ownership, where current-main history points most strongly to steipete.
